reasoning: Set A wins. Its plan is tighter and easier to build from. Both sets cover all three environments with a shared core, hand-written learners, baselines, replay and statistics. Set B has the richer RL design: a REINFORCE → actor-critic → PPO ladder with ablation switches, test environments (corridor, line, chase) that prove the core, a self-play ladder and cross-play tables. That design costs B a lot of clarity. Its brief still frames the second environment as 'whatever it is' although the roadmap and spec plan the fish tank. Its architecture keeps process narration ('Nothing is built yet (M1 has 0 of 22 tasks done)', 'the build waits for … replan') and leaves the statistical test 'to the skill', while the pipelines already fix one-sided paired tests with Bonferroni. PL-01 is a 34-row step table that also lists hunt, schedule and scripted-predator rows, so you can't sketch the entry function from it. The plan's IDs run out of order (T20–T24 come before T14), and four DQN thicken tasks on separate files are chained for no file reason. M1 also gives no way to watch the agent. Set A's milestones are clearer. M1 is a true walking skeleton (train and watch a snake), the interface freezes compact code-shaped types with fakes, the todo runs in order, and it decides its statistics and chart style (AD-20, AD-21). A has real faults too. Its brief allows a paid cloud GPU and lowers the fish bar to 'at least match the scripted fish'. Its pipeline doc still says 'the null-hypothesis-testing skill's test' and 'as the dataviz skill specifies', and the load_policy spine still reads 'torch.load the state dict' after AD-15 changed the saved form. M3 packs the whole fish-tank stage into one lopsided milestone, and AD-22 keeps process narration. On balance A is more consistent, right-sized and buildable.

strengths: M1 is a real walking skeleton: train a snake, then record and watch it
The contract is compact, with code-shaped types, named samples and fixture-backed fakes for each boundary
Statistics and chart style are decided concretely (AD-20 paired sign-flip test with Holm correction; AD-21 Okabe–Ito chart)
Well-argued RL choices: Double DQN, the reason the Snake observation must hold more than the scripted snake sees, and a tanh-squashed Gaussian for heading
The todo, plan and roadmap agree on what comes next, and IDs run in order
weaknesses: The brief and spec allow a paid cloud GPU (QR-02), which breaks the free-tools constraint
The fish only need to 'at least match' the scripted fish, weaker than the ground-truth bar
The pipeline doc keeps superseded text: skill references, `torch.load the state dict`, and `iterate until the time limit`
M3 packs the whole fish stage (single fish, five fish, PPO, SB3 reference, sign-off) into one lopsided milestone
Process narration sits in architecture AD-22 and in the plan's replan notes

strengths: The deepest RL pedagogy: a policy-gradient ladder, ablation switches, and a self-play ladder with cross-play tables
The shared core is proven on small test environments (corridor, line, chase) and runs unchanged when the core grows (CORE-09)
Free tools only, CPU only, and every learner must beat both baselines, matching the ground truth
Very detailed spec with exact numbers and edge cases
weaknesses: Heavily bloated: a 34-row PL-01, a contract with 132 headings, and packets that repeat the whole PL-01 table
Stale framing in the brief ('The second environment, whatever it is') and process narration in the architecture
The statistical method is left 'to the skill' in Risks while the pipelines already fix Bonferroni
The plan lists tasks out of ID order, and the DQN thicken tasks are falsely serialized
Milestones are layered by function (train, then baselines/curves/replay, then study); M1 can't be watched
An open question admits the import-linter layers may block M1-T01's gate
